work: Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning
heading: Liji 13 · Sang Fu Xiao Ji 喪服小記 · Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning · Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.46 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.50

items.text: Perform the mourning rites for his father: bind up his hair, bare his chest, descend to the court and leap, then cover his chest and put on the sash.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.46–50
items.quote: bound up his hair in the raised hall, bared his chest, descended to the court, and there performed his leaping.

items.text: Perform the mourning rites for his mother: do not bind up his hair, but bare his chest, descend to the court and leap, then cover his chest and put on the cincture.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.46–50
items.quote: If the rites were for his mother, he did not bind up his hair. He bared his chest, however, in the hall, descended to the court, and went through his leaping.

items.text: Wear five months' mourning for a departed daughter-in-law when the eldest son and his wife could not take the place of his parents.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.46–50
items.quote: When an eldest son and his wife could not take the place hereafter of his parents, her mother-in-law wore for her only the five months' mourning.

work: Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning
heading: Liji 13 · Sang Fu Xiao Ji 喪服小記 · Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning · Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.24

items.text: If your concubine bore you a son, wear three months' mourning for her; if she had no son, do not mourn.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: When the concubine of an officer had a son, he wore the three months' mourning for her.
items.conflict: Concubinage (polygamy) conflicts with monogamous marriage (Gen 2:24; 1 Cor 7:2).

items.text: Mourn for the ruler's eldest son for the same time as his wife, the son's mother, does.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: For the ruler's eldest son a concubine wore mourning for the same time as his wife, (the son's mother).

items.text: Do not reduce the mourning for your father even if your grandfather reduced mourning for that son.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: but his grandson, (the son of that son), did not reduce his mourning for his father.

items.text: If your husband has become the successor of another man, wear nine months' mourning for his adoptive parents.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: his wife wore the nine months' mourning for his parents-in-law.

items.text: Mourn for your stepfather only if you lived together, both lacked sons, and he shared his resources and enabled you to sacrifice to your ancestors.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: must have lived together and both be without sons to preside at their mourning rites; and (the stepfather moreover) must have shared his resources

items.text: As head of your new branch, complete the full mourning for your wife even if your mother is alive.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: completed the full period of mourning for his wife.

items.text: When mourning both parents, do not offer the sacrifice of repose or enshrine the tablet for your mother buried first until after your father's burial.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: the sacrifices of repose and of the enshrining of the tablet, for the (mother) who was buried first, did not take place till after the burial of the father.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is not commanded in Scripture; worship belongs to God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If you direct mourning rites for one who must mourn three years while you yourself owe only nine months, offer the two annual terminal sacrifices on their behalf.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: he should offer for them the two annual terminal sacrifices.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is not commanded in Scripture; worship belongs to God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If you are a concubine's son reared by another concubine, act as a son to her.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.23–II.24
items.quote: might act as son to that other
items.conflict: Concubinage/polygamy; honoring a non-parent as mother conflicts with honoring one's own parents (Exod 20:12; Eph 6:1-2).
items.needs_role: concubine's son reared by another concubine

work: Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning
heading: Liji 13 · Sang Fu Xiao Ji 喪服小記 · Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning · Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.45

items.text: Wear mourning for them as if they had died young when they die childless after coming of age.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: if they died childless, those who would have presided at their rites wore the mourning for them which they would then have done

items.text: If the burial is delayed, do not put off your mourning until it takes place, even if others finish after the set months.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: he who was presiding over the mourning rites was the only one who did not put off his mourning

items.text: Wear the hair-pin of arrow-bamboo for your father to the end of the three years' mourning.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: The hair-pin of the arrow-bamboo was worn by (an unmarried daughter for her father) to the end of the three years' mourning.

items.text: At the first-year sacrifice, consult the divining stalks for the day and the personator; at the second-year, wear court robes and divine about the personator.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: they consulted the divining stalks about the day for it, and the individual who was to act as personator
items.conflict: Scripture forbids divination; trust God to order times (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: If your father is alive and lives with you, do not perform the end-of-mourning sacrifice for your mother or carry a staff when going to wail for her.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: The son of a concubine, living in the same house with his father, did not observe the sacrifice... Nor did such a son carry his staff

items.text: When tending a sick relative, lay aside your mourning clothes; if the sick one is your superior, change them, but you need not for a junior.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: One who was ministering to another who was ill did not do so in the mourning clothes... In ministering to one more honourable than himself, the rule required a person to change

items.text: At the sacrifices of repose and the ending of wailing for your wife, preside if you can; otherwise your son should preside, but her father-in-law presides when her tablet is placed.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: In the mourning rites for a wife, at the sacrifices of repose and on the ending of the wailing, her husband or son presided; when her tablet was put in its place, her father-in-law presided.
items.conflict: Ancestral tablets and offerings to the dead conflict with worshiping God alone (Exod. 20:3-5).

items.text: Do not preside at the mourning rites for a Great officer unless you are the direct descendant of the Honoured Head of your branch.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: An (ordinary) officer did not take the place of presiding (at the mourning rites) for a Great officer. It was only when he was the direct descendant

items.text: If your cousin arrives from another state before you have put off your mourning, receive him as host but without the mourning cincture.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: If a cousin arrived from another state, before the presiding mourner had put off his mourning, the latter received him in the part of host, but without the mourning cincture.

items.text: When you arrive after the burial of your brother or cousin, go first to the grave and then to the house to wail.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: Parties hurrying to the mourning rites for a brother or cousin... first went to the grave and afterwards to the house

items.text: When mourning a son other than your eldest by your wife, do not pass the night in the shed outside the middle door.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: A father (at the mourning rites) for any of his other sons did not pass the night in the shed outside

items.text: If your mother was divorced, do not wear mourning for her, because one engaged in mourning rites cannot offer sacrifice.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji II.25
items.quote: A son who was or would be his fathers successor did not wear mourning for his divorced mother. He did not wear such mourning, because one engaged in mourning rites could not offer sacrifice.
items.conflict: Honor your mother regardless of her marital status; ancestor sacrifice is not the ground of mourning (Exod. 20:12; Mark 7:10-13).

work: Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning
heading: Liji 13 · Sang Fu Xiao Ji 喪服小記 · Record Of Smaller Matters In The Dress Of Mourning · Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22

items.text: Wear unhemmed sackcloth and a hempen hairband when mourning your father and mother; for your mother, exchange the band for a linen cincture.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: When wearing the unhemmed sackcloth (for a father), (the son) tied up his hair with a hempen (band), and also when wearing it for a mother.

items.text: Mourn your grandmother for three years if your grandfather is already dead and you are the representative of the family.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: When the grandfather was dead, and afterwards (the grandson) had to go into mourning for his grandmother, he, being the representative of the family (through the death of his father), did so for three years.

items.text: At the mourning rites for your father or mother, lay your forehead to the ground before bowing to a visitor who has come to condole.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: The eldest son (at the mourning rites) for his father or mother, (before bowing to a visitor who had come to condole with him), first laid his forehead to the ground (as an expression of his sorrow).

items.text: At the rites for your husband, bow your head to the ground before you salute a visitor.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: A wife, at the rites for her husband or eldest son, bowed her head to the ground before she saluted a visitor

items.text: At the rites for your eldest son, bow your head to the ground before you salute a visitor.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: A wife, at the rites for her husband or eldest son, bowed her head to the ground before she saluted a visitor

items.text: If you are your father's successor as head of the family, do not wear mourning for your mother who has been divorced.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: The son who was his father's successor (as now head of the family) did not wear mourning for his mother who had been divorced.

items.text: Revere the Honoured Head of your branch, for this is the way you honor the ancestor and his immediate successor.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: Because they honoured the ancestor, they reverenced the Honoured Head

items.text: As the Honoured Head, offer sacrifice to your grandfather; no other son may do so.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: any other son but the eldest did not sacrifice to his grandfather

items.text: As the Honoured Head, wear the three years' unhemmed sackcloth for your eldest son, because he continues the direct line.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: no son but he wore the (three years) unhemmed sackcloth for his eldest son, because the eldest son of no other continued (the direct line) of the grandfather and father.

items.text: As the heir-son, do not diminish the mourning for the parents of your wife.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: The heir-son (of the king or a feudal lord) did not diminish the mourning for the parents of his wife.

items.text: Perform the great royal sacrifice to all ancestors, giving first place to him from whom the founder sprang, with the founder as assessor.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: the first place was given to him from whom the founder of the line sprang, and that founder had the place of assessor to him.

items.text: If you are a concubine who left with the divorced wife, do not wear mourning for your son.
items.citation: Liji, Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.1 … Sang Fu Xiao Ji I.22
items.quote: the concubine, (following her out of the harem), did not wear mourning for her son.
items.conflict: Mothers must mourn their children; concubinage violates monogamy (Genesis 2:24)
